## Overview

The world is called **Aetris** — an ancient name that evokes echoes of a time before time, whispered in the root of words for "ancient" and for "triad" or "three." It is a fitting name, for the number three recurs throughout the world's deepest truths: three Originals, three capital cities, three stabilizing planes (the Anchors), and the threefold nature of magic itself.

The world of Aetris comprises **three known continents**. The campaign takes place primarily on **Kythoria** — a vast landmass of diverse climates and terrains, stretching from frozen northern reaches to subtropical southern shores. The other two continents exist but remain distant and scarcely known to the peoples of Kythoria; their details are left deliberately undefined for now.

---

## The Continent of Kythoria

Kythoria is the cradle of mortal civilization — and the stage upon which the greatest drama of recent history has unfolded. It is a continent of striking diversity, shaped by the same primordial forces that gave birth to all the planes.

### Regions & Climate

Kythoria spans multiple climate zones, creating distinct regions with their own character and challenges:

#### The Frozen North (Arctic / Subarctic)
The northern reaches of Kythoria are a harsh, cold expanse of tundra, taiga, and snow-capped mountains. The cold is biting, the growing season short, and the nights long. Before the monster invasion, hardy dwarf holds and human settlements dotted this region. Today, much of the north remains under monster control, its frozen wastes serving as a near-impenetrable stronghold for the enemy. The rare expeditions that venture north return with tales of blizzards that seem almost sentient and creatures that have adapted to the cold in horrifying ways.

#### The Temperate Heartlands
The center of the continent enjoys a temperate climate — four distinct seasons, fertile farmlands, rolling hills, and dense forests. This is where the three capital cities of the Last Stand — **Skywatch**, **Emberforge**, and **Weaveheart** — were founded near the center-southeast. The heartlands are the most densely populated and safest region of the continent. The soil is rich, the rivers run clean, and the forests, while still holding pockets of danger, have been largely reconquered and resettled. This region also contains the **ley line convergence** beneath Weaveheart — a place where the raw essence of B's sacrifice flows close to the surface.

#### The Subtropical South
The southern coast of Kythoria enjoys a warm, subtropical climate with mild winters, long summers, and abundant rainfall. Dense jungles, mangrove swamps, and white-sand beaches define this region. The south was one of the first regions fully recovered after the Last Stand, and its ports are vital for trade. Exotic fruits, rare spices, and unique timber are exported from here. The jungles still hide ancient ruins — pre-invasion cities swallowed by vegetation, now being slowly reclaimed by settlers and adventurers alike.

#### The Eastern Coast & Sea Routes
The eastern seaboard of Kythoria is a vital artery for trade and travel. Safe sea lanes connect the major ports, allowing goods, people, and information to flow between the southern ports and the central heartlands. The sea is patrolled, but piracy and rogue monster activity remain occasional threats. The eastern coast was recovered early in the reconquering and is now a thriving network of port towns, fishing villages, and trading posts.

#### The Western Frontier
The west is where the reconquering effort is most active. This contested zone marks the boundary between reclaimed territory and monster-held lands. The terrain transitions from the temperate farmlands of the heartlands into rugged highlands, deep forests, and eventually the unknown reaches of the far west — lands that have been under monster control for four centuries. The frontier is dotted with military outposts, forward operating bases, and fledgling settlements established by the brave (or the desperate).

---

## The Eras of Kythoria

The history of mortal civilization on Kythoria is divided into three broad eras, with the fourth — the present — still being written.

### Era of Foundation (before 400 years ago)
*The ancient past, prior to historical record.*

This era encompasses the time from the arrival of the mortal races on the Material Plane up until the monster invasion. Much has been lost to time. The great kingdoms, the original racial homelands, the cultures and wonders of this age — all lie buried beneath four centuries of war and ruin. Few records survive. What is known is pieced together from fragments of ancient texts, ruins, and oral traditions passed down through the generations. This era is left intentionally open to allow for future development and player backstory integration.

### The Abominable End (400 — 200 years ago)
*A name whispered in dread — the century of suffering.*

Approximately **400 years ago**, an ever-growing tide of monsters began appearing at the fringes of Kythoria. Their numbers were endless, their origins unknown. They pushed inward relentlessly, consuming territory and driving the mortal races before them. For two centuries, civilization crumbled. Kingdoms fell. Cities were overrun. The mortal races were pushed to the brink of extinction, clinging to the center-southeast of the continent as their last hope. This era is remembered as **The Abominable End** — a time of unimaginable cruelty and suffering, when hope itself seemed to die.

### The Rise of the Mortals (200 years ago — Present)
*A new dawn forged in unity and defiance.*

**200 years ago**, the surviving mortal races made their final stand. The three capital cities — Skywatch, Emberforge, and Weaveheart — were founded near the center-southeast of the continent. Together, they became known as **the Last Stand**. A magical barrier was developed in Weaveheart, powered by the ley line convergence, creating a safe haven from the monster hordes.

From this bastion, the mortal races organized and began to **reconquer** their lost lands. This era, called **The Rise of the Mortals**, represents the slow, determined reclamation of Kythoria. The south and east have been recovered. Trade routes — both sea and land — have been re-established. Civilization is rebuilding. But the north and west remain contested, and approximately one-third of the continent still lies under monster control.

---

## State of Civilization

### Recovered Territories (South & East)
The recovered lands of southern and eastern Kythoria are home to a mix of:
- **Large settlements** — thriving towns and cities rebuilt on the foundations of older ones
- **Small villages** — farming communities, fishing hamlets, and logging camps
- **Reclaimed ruins** — ancient sites being excavated and resettled, with monster-hunting contracts still active to clear remaining threats

### Trade & Travel
- **Sea routes** connect the eastern and southern coasts, forming the primary trade network
- **Land roads** are being re-established between settlements, with caravans traveling under guard
- Trade is vital — goods, resources, and information flow between the capitals and the recovered territories

### The Frontier
The boundary between recovered and monster-held lands is marked by:
- **A major forward operating base** — a fortified settlement serving as the Last Stand army's command center for reconquering operations
- **Smaller frontier settlements** — established by settlers pushing outward, often protected by a palisade and a small garrison
- **Ruins and dungeons** — monster-occupied structures from the pre-invasion era, containing dangerous beasts, lost treasures, and the currency of fallen civilizations. The Last Stand army issues contracts for clearing these sites, which serves both to reclaim territory and to recover resources for the war effort

### Adventuring Context
The state of Kythoria creates a natural environment for adventurers:
- **Monster-hunting contracts** issued by the Last Stand army and local settlements to clear ruins, dungeons, and monster lairs
- **Dungeon delving** — ancient ruins still hold treasures, magical items, and the accumulated wealth of pre-invasion kingdoms. This explains why dungeons contain coins, magic items, and other valuables
- **Frontier exploration** — pushing into contested or unknown territories to scout, map, and establish new footholds
- **Trade protection** — guarding caravans and ships traveling the re-established trade routes

## Open Questions

- **Calendar & Time**: A custom calendar system is desired (5-day weeks, 10 months, 4 weeks per month = 200 days per year, with custom weekday names). To be developed in a future update.
- **Era of Foundation**: The pre-invasion era will be detailed further when needed for plot or backstory development.
- **Specific Locations**: Individual towns, forests, rivers, mountains, and other geographical features to be named and detailed as needed.

## Thematic Notes

The name **Aetris** is deliberately chosen to evoke both "ancient" (aeon, aeternal) and "three" (tri-, tres). This triple theme runs throughout the setting:
- **Three Originals** (A, B, C)
- **Three capital cities** (Skywatch, Emberforge, Weaveheart)
- **Three Anchors** (Feywild, Shadowfell, Ethereal Plane)
- **Three eras** (Foundation, Abominable End, Rise of the Mortals)
- **Threefold magic** (Arcane, Divine, Primal)

The continent **Kythoria** is home to all mortal races, their fates intertwined by shared survival and the ongoing reconquering of their ancestral lands.
